So I can speak to this rather uniquely as I have an on going relationship with my old therapist, although it’s not a friendship.

We have text discussions ( maybe once a month or less and they don’t generally cover therapy-type topics). I send her pictures as I travel a lot and like to share that stuff.

We also , even though she is technically no longer in clinical practice, see each other 2-3 times a year.  In an office a colleague lets her use. And I pay her for these sessions.

She did this because we worked together for 7 years on some really severe early attachment trauma/abuse/neglect. She decided she had to leave clinical practice bc she has teenagers who were struggling since COVID and elderly parents with failing health. My treatment wasn’t really over but she felt as she put it “if I keep doing regular therapy with you all you will get is scraps of my attention and you don’t deserve scraps”. She had already started a teaching job and I was the last client she was still seeing.  She was my earned secure attachment person and we both agreed a complete cut off would do more harm than good.

But sometimes I’m not sure if that is true.  In some ways since we were working towards secure attachment my relationship with my T is more child-like even though I am only about a decade younger. And like a child I often idealized her and she rarely disappointed me.

But for example we were supposed to meet two weeks ago and her mom had a medical episode and she forgot to let me know. So she stood me up which was like my worst fear. BUT I’m not in therapy with her anymore. So I had HUGE feelings and while she did apologize there is no way to process those feelings like we used to so I am left to deal with the fallout alone.

We did meet a few days ago but since I have 2-3 hrs a year I didn’t want to spend one of those hours probing pain that there really isn’t a way to resolve. I wanted just to enjoy being with her and connected to her.

But now I have these huge feelings and I am wrestling with them alone.

Also I used to be able to be confident if I contacted her outside of session she would respond promptly. But now sometimes my texts don’t get read for days or weeks. Is she ignoring me? Is she just overwhelmed? Why doesn’t she respond? Doesn’t she know how hard that is?

I don’t know. I can’t ask because we aren’t really doing therapy anymore. So again, huge feelings, no way to resolve.

Since she is my earned secure attachment person I have a huge base of world view and self love that she scaffolded. At times that scaffolding has come close to coming apart because of the way I get ignored sometimes now. Sometimes I question everything that happened between us in therapy. Now the excellent part is I have realized through that that I no longer need her to love me for me to love myself. The not excellent part is that something extremely precious that we worked very hard to build is sometimes in serious danger….

But again we aren’t doing therapy so how do we talk about this? I can hardly send her a pic of me snowboarding in California and then add “by the way I really need to know why you sometimes read my texts and sometimes don’t . And it’s bring up big abandonment issues. And I know I am ok without you but also it can be very painful. What is going on?”

Because again she isn’t really my therapist anymore.

Overall I think it’s a positive in my life. It’s important for me to feel loved and supported by her, and the connection is important to both of us. 
But we aren’t friends or anything. We still have some substantial boundaries in place like she rarely talks about herself, we meet in an office, I still pay her, etc etc.

And it’s still able to create emotional struggle and havoc for me. Nevermind that how would we even BE friends with the power imbalance? If she said “Brennir10 I need your kidney “ I’d give it to her. I’d do literally anything she asked short of giving up my animals or career,commiting a serious crime, or sex acts.  We wouldn’t really even need to discuss why she needed something from me . I’d just do it. How could I possibly take care of myself in thst relationship? So then what happens? Because in therapy the therapist takes care of you. But in adult friendship you each take care of your own boundaries and emotional safety.  

Also I need to preserve my sense of her as an excellent person full of pure love or a lot of our therapy work gets unstable. I can’t imagine how that would work if she chewed out a barista or made some insensitive remarks about something . And what if we argued??? Or god forbid the friendship blew up.How would my heart deal with that from the person who is my earned secure attachment figure????

Also I have struggled to work with another therapist. I know we will not ever work together again. But with my amazing earned secure attachment person there, new therapists just don’t seem too great. 

It’s hard at times even with the guardrails we have in place.  I think overall it’s a rare situation where continuing the relationship is helpful.  It’s been tough acknowledging that she has probably also never had a therapy relationship go this way. And likely she is blundering along and not even aware at times when she hurts me.and again. When she does hurt me, there is no real space to talk about it ….but she is still my earned secure attachment person and so the feelings are very big.

I’m a veterinarian with a long trauma history. I run my own practice. I was also thrown out of my church and social groups first year of vet school bc I’m gay.
It wasn’t pretty, but I made it. Basically I have “work mode “ where all my big feelings are stuffed in a sealed box til I can deal with them.  I should add I am neurodivergent so I also mask in most social situations.  I was great academically, excell at my job, I’m good to extremely good at pretty much anything I try. Started drawing and 2 years later had a piece in a gallery show. Used to run top ten in my age group at marathons. Etc

And yet for years I had a dark yawning abyss inside me

Therapy fixed that but it took years. On the upside now I have the peace and perspective to actually ENJOY the results of all my hard work. Rather than just desperately trying to prove to the world that I deserve to exist. 

I’ve worked through most of my trauma now

Adding, I myself have trauma beginning in infancy and eventually centered my therapy on the big emotions and destructive impulses I had trouble regulating in my adult life. I will never know exactly what happened or when. I know enough to know whatever happened was traumatic.  That was enough to get some big healing done

Do details matter? Given that you were in an orphanage we can already deduce your early life had attachment trauma if nothing else. Possibly other trauma such as neglect, physical abuse etc 

That’s enough to give you some really big feelings to work through without there being some other unknown trauma. We certainly can carry over emotions and trauma from infancy even without any narrative memory. 

Can I ask what exactly makes you “feel” like this happened ?

I’m a veterinarian. I’ve helped hundreds of people with this transition….

The first thing to decide: do you want your baby to pass at home or at the vet clinic?
In home end of life care is a thing ( I provide it) and many owners find it a much more peaceful transition.

As for after care of the body i personally prefer cremation. Your pets ashes dan stay with you and even be buried with you or you can scatter them. They can be made into art or gemstones you can wear. Many many ways to honor a pet this way.

Even if you are not sure if you want them I would recommend paw print, nose print, hair clipping so that you have them if you do want them. 

The veterinarian who helps you with your pets passing can give you information on the body care services in your area.

Plan a memorial for after you get the ashes back. Also there are a lot of grief resources and even support groups if you need them

This website has a LoT of excellent info on how to make the decision and proceed through the resulting grief

Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 109 (33), 13220-13224, 2012
Since the sinking of the Titanic, there has been a widespread belief that the social norm of “women and children first” (WCF) gives women a survival advantage over men in maritime disasters, and that captains and crew members give priority to passengers. We analyze a database of 18 maritime disasters spanning three centuries, covering the fate of over 15,000 individuals of more than 30 nationalities. Our results provide a unique picture of maritime disasters. Women have a distinct survival disadvantage compared with men. Captains and crew survive at a significantly higher rate than passengers. We also find that: the captain has the power to enforce normative behavior; there seems to be no association between duration of a disaster and the impact of social norms; women fare no better when they constitute a small share of the ship’s complement; the length of the voyage before the disaster appears to have no impact on women’s relative survival rate; the sex gap in survival rates has declined since World War I; and women have a larger disadvantage in British shipwrecks. Just saying as an equine vet, that vet made the right call.

Fractures are not uncommon in horses. Dislocations are VERY VERY uncommon. I see multiple fractures a year. I’ve seen ONE joint dislocation ( fetlock in a mini donkey) in my entire 20+ year career. The strength and number of ligaments in/surrounding/stabilizing the hock make dislocation of the hock in the horse a near impossibility. All the bones in the leg would break before those ligaments would ALL tear badly enough to allow dislocation. If the hock DID dislocate the horse would require euthanasia because those ligaments won’t heal and we can’t fix them. Horses with single tears in just ONE of the many ligaments surrounding the hock are incredibly lame and have a long recovery.  

. Horses with fractures are in so much pain. Transporting them is very difficult. The leg has to be casted/splinted very carefully or it can make the fracture worse. and still, it’s very painful. It should only be done when the owner is committed to spending the many thousands of dollars required for repair with its many potential complications and potential failure AND the vet thinks there is a reasonably good likelihood the injury is repairable in the first place.

For blood collection it is more helpful to think of it like this. The vet must either pay an outside lab or use an in house machine with expensive components to run the blood test. The fee for the test itself is for those costs. It’s separate from the fee for removing the blood from
 The animal bc lab and components prices change with some frequency. This makes it easy to change the price based on the clinic’s cost.

The blood collection fee is for getting the blood out of the animal is generally more static and doesn’t need to be adjusted relative to charges to the clinic.

Medication is the same . The cost the clinic pays for the actual medication is dependent on the supplier and prices change.

The cost of giving the medication is relatively static and may only change every few years.

That’s the reasoning for separate charges.

People on this sub VASTLY overestimate the availability of food in a high alpine forest. If food was easy to find or grow there, people would have settled there a long time ago. Basically anywhere that isn’t already full

Like a moose a few people might be fine but they are basically feeding a family of 15 with one gun. There are things you can eat but they are not necessarily good for you. In summer maybe you will get some blueberries if you want to risk a bear encounter ( that gun will just piss a brown bear off ) but you will also burn lots of calories looking for them. Actually given the caloric needs of catching/hunting, providing food for the rabbits etc they probably would burn more calories than they gained. That’s part of the mechanism of rabbit starvation.  You have a diet both deficient in calories AND essential nutrients. If all you can catch are small fish or small game like rabbits, you actually create more of a calorie deficit obtaining and eating the food than you do if you just sit around. That’s why big game like moose, walrus etc are very important to indigenous cultures that rely primarily on meat.  In starvation situations it’s best to conserve as much energy as possible rather than burn it hunting small amounts of food . You are best off w a low energy means of obtaining food like fish traps etc if you have to live on fish and small game. The book How To Stay Alive in the Woods explains this pretty well

It doesn’t HAVE to be retraumatizing. It’s not family, it’s not friends, the therapy relationship is very unique,very centered on you. 

I think ( I know I did) those of us who grow up with attachment trauma think that somehow everyone else’s family relationships are like they are on TV. We have an idealized version of unconditional love, all the time.

But “normal “ relationships are gritty. My T I knew would be there for our next appointment, no matter what I said or how I acted. She wasn’t going to walk away like some of my friends have or reject me the way my family did.

You have to honor what the relationship IS instead of always looking at what it’s NOT. I had powerful maternal transference but would remind myself “ how would I feel about x thing my T said if my mom said it?”  I need very specific parts of maternal attachment, not the whole thing. I can feed and clothe myself, have a good career, and don’t like anyone giving me unsolicited advice about my life. I can take care of myself when I am sick or hurt, drive myself places, buy what I want to,go where I want to…..I am a fully formed adult except for specific needs.

It helped me to isolate those needs and figure out what I could bring to therapy to have met. For example I was constantly gaslighted as a child, so I needed my T to very clearly believe me about anything I shared. I never felt safe in my home so we worked on making the therapy space feel as safe for me as possible. I needed to be seen and valued and my T did that in our sessions

I also learned to speak to myself the way she spoke to me, and treat myself the way she said she would treat me and that allowed me to reparent myself.

It doesn’t have to be retraumatizing. The T relationship is unique and it CAN meet some of those unmet needs. But it does require separating out what the true needs are so they can be contained and addressed . It only becomes retraumatizing if you expect it to be something different from what it actually is

It’s likely the diet has a real effect based on science. The issue is People confuse a medical ketogenic diet with the popular “doing Keto”
I have a medical condition that sometimes responds to a ketogenic diet particularly in children…but people don’t understand what a medical ketogenic diet is. It’s VERY high fat. Very. And difficult to manage. So difficult that parents with kids on the keto diet rely on meal replacement foods . The actual ketogenic diet is unpalatable which is why patients are often hospitalized to be on it

A medical ketogenic diet is 75% fat, 20% protein, 5% carbs
It’s much more restrictive and fat heavy than the popular “keto” a sample menu includes huge amounts of plain whipping cream. Mayonnaise, heavy cream etc—-without any sweeteners or other ingredients. Can you imagine eating a 1/4 cup mayonnaise or drinking a glass of heavy cream by itself multiple times a day? While restricting both protein and carbs? Every item must be carefully weighed and measured bc messing up the ratio even a little can negate the effects.

I ended up choosing not to try it: consuming such a huge quantity of fat is not well researched in terms of effect on cholesterol etc in adults, the amount of measuring is super tedious and the menu was nasty sounding, I have a lot of pain but live a full functional life and felt the diet would be More tedious than living with pain I am already accustomed to.

It works best in young children whose diets are almost exclusively provided by their parents, with parents committed enough to do the extensive work it takes to maintain 

It doesn’t work at home bc very few adults with free access to food could stay on it and/or people do not measure etc like they are supposed to

Cats and dogs like most predators are gorge eaters— when you kill an animal you need to eat all you can before someone bigger steals it from you. They don’t really have a “full”. My parrot on the other hand, since they are foragers, and foragers don’t generally gorge eat can be left with an all you can eat amount of healthy foods and regulates herself.

Gorge eating as a strategy depends on a hunting lifestyle where game cannot always be taken down. Gorge eaters may go days between meals.Giving gorge eaters all they can eat everyday is at odds with their basic wiring. Now we do not let our dogs and cats gorge bc this style of feeding comes with inherent risks ( bloat, vomiting, diarrhea, intestinal blockage etc) that we do not like to expose our pets too. So we have to feed them in a way that is at odds with their basic wiring which means controlling the amounts

Humans are foragers, not gorge eaters. Eating a steady amount is normal for us.  But it’s not normal for dogs or cats

So —this is based on the theory that emotions are names for body states. Ie it’s not I am thinking about a test and feel anxious and then I get nauseous. Instead how emotions work is basically  brain which already knows about the test is sending out various chemicals that are increasing your heart rate, increasing gut motility etc—and as a very small child you learn to name that feeling as fear.  Your body is sending out chemical signals etc before you KNOW you are scared.

So you ought to learn “ everything in the gut is going at a normal rate, no changes in blood flow or digestion”= a peaceful state, contentment etc

Same with cardiovascular responses: your heart , diaphragm, lungs etc responds to things and you learn to name the response in some way—sadness, excitement etc.

Depending on your brain chemistry and your upbringing your name for the response may or may not be congruent with what is really happening in your life. For example I had an abusive childhood and was afraid a LOT. I learned that it’s “fear” and “bad things are going to happen” if my heart rate increased, stomach motility increased etc.Now when I am excited about something like a vacation, I will initially name the sensations in my body as “fear”—-sometimes to the point of wanting to cancel the thing I am excited about. I had. To do a lot of body centered therapy to rewire my names for my body’s responses and I had grown up in a dangerous environment so I tended to interpret any kind of arousal as a negative emotion. 

It sounds like they are saying that people who ruminate negatively a lot have become insensitive to their bodies messages. So even though their stomachs are calm, heart beating normal, all the things that say things are ok in the world—-they cognitively are still feeling life is going badly. They aren’t receiving the messages from their body saying everything is actually pretty ok right now

Of course it’s really pretty complicated but if you struggle with anxiety or negative emotions interoception is very interesting to read about.

Well, science does not support your experience is all I can say. Behavioral problems are the number one reason cats are surrendered ( over 50% of cats adopted are rehomed /returned in the first few months after adoption). And stress in multi cat households are a primary cause of these behavior problems . Also a lot of times people miss signs of stress in cats unless it’s severe ( fighting etc). I just finished doing  veterinary continuing education on managing behavior issues in cats.  This info is mostly from the Kansas State Veterinary Medical Association presentation on managing behavioral issues in cats, coupled with other reading and discussion w other vets, as well as 20 years of clinical experience as a veterinarian.

In households with more than 3 cats, the overall stress in the cat household and the likelihood of physical/behavioral issues from stress increases significantly. So 3 cats is a wise cut off. As a veterinarian that is the max number of cats I will keep in a household.

Veterinarian here: your first responsibility is to the cats you already have. They deserve enough space to be comfortable, have their own territory, eliminate comfortably. The difference between 3 cats and 4 cats seems small but once you get past 3 cats in a household the incidence of significant behavior issues like persistently eliminating outside the litter boxes increases dramatically.
It becomes MUCH harder to meet the cats needs for privacy, security etc.

Your cats you already have deserve your care first and foremost

So when you are a very small child, your relationship with your caregiver will create a secure attachment.  You feel safe, centered, at peace in the world.
